title_bn: Hridoy, Litton lift Bangladesh to record 327/6 after Rabada five-for
title_en: Hridoy, Litton lift Bangladesh to record 327/6 after Rabada five-for
summary_bn: He then had Mominul Haque caught behind and bowled captain Najmul Hossain Shanto with an inswinging full delivery, leaving Bangladesh on 22 for three in the ninth over.
summary_en: He then had Mominul Haque caught behind and bowled captain Najmul Hossain Shanto with an inswinging full delivery, leaving Bangladesh on 22 for three in the ninth over.
body_bn:
He then had Mominul Haque caught behind and bowled captain Najmul Hossain Shanto with an inswinging full delivery, leaving Bangladesh on 22 for three in the ninth over.

Towhid Hridoy struck 137 and shared a record 206-run stand with Litton Das to lift Bangladesh to 327 for six on the opening day of the first Test against South Africa in Johannesburg today (15 November).

It is Bangladesh's highest total against South Africa in Tests. Litton will resume on 92 on the second day.

Hridoy was lbw to Marco Jansen off the last ball of the day, ending a sixth-wicket stand that is now Bangladesh's highest against South Africa, home or away.

The previous best was 138, by Jaker Ali and Mehidy Hasan Miraz for the seventh wicket in Mirpur in 2024.

The pair came together after Kagiso Rabada had taken all five Bangladesh wickets to fall, reducing them to 121 for five.

Rabada struck with the first ball of the match, when debutant Mahfizul Islam was caught by Jansen at gully.

He then had Mominul Haque caught behind and bowled captain Najmul Hossain Shanto with an inswinging full delivery, leaving Bangladesh on 22 for three in the ninth over.

Tanzid Hasan and Hridoy rebuilt with a 99-run stand for the fourth wicket, the highest by a Bangladesh pair in South Africa at the time. It beat the 84 by Hannan Sarkar and Habibul Bashar in Potchefstroom in 2002.

Both survived chances. Aiden Markram, no, Ackermann at point got a hand to a catch off Tanzid from Jansen's bowling but could not hold it, and a Hridoy edge off Wiaan Mulder fell just short of third slip.

Tanzid reached his second Test fifty before lunch, but Rabada returned after the break to remove him and Mushfiqur Rahim off successive balls. Tanzid dragged a bouncer onto his stumps, and Mushfiqur was caught at third slip first ball.

It was Rabada's 18th five-wicket haul in Tests, and he became the first bowler to take five wickets in an innings five times against Bangladesh.

Hridoy and Litton then took control. They passed Bangladesh's first 100-run partnership on South African soil less than two hours after the Tanzid-Hridoy record, and batted through the rest of the day until Hridoy's dismissal.

Hridoy, playing only his fourth Test, became the second Bangladesh batter to score a Test century against South Africa. He has now passed fifty in three consecutive Test innings, after scoring an unbeaten 242 and 82 in the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet.

Litton reached his 22nd Test fifty off 71 balls.

Bangladesh chose to bat after Shanto won the toss, fielding three pacers and one spinner.

summary_en: Filmmaker Sohel Rahman has completed his first feature film, 'Hawar Gaari' (The Wind Car). It tells the story of working-class life in Dhaka and the unequal fight against cancer, with love, hope and resilience at its heart. The film was produced under the banner of Vila Do Cinema. Its final cut was finished in November
body_bn:
Filmmaker Sohel Rahman has completed his first feature film, 'Hawar Gaari' (The Wind Car). It tells the story of working-class life in Dhaka and the unequal fight against cancer, with love, hope and resilience at its heart.

The film was produced under the banner of Vila Do Cinema. Its final cut was finished in November after four months of editing in Portugal and Spain. It is due for release early next year, though no date has been announced.

Chitralekha Guha, Fazlul Haque, Ayman Shimla, Yashfa Tasnia Mallick, Omar Faruque, Tridha Paul Maan and Shobdo play the leading roles.

The story comes from a tragedy in the director's own life. A month after their wedding, his wife, Dr Shamrina Tanha, was diagnosed with cancer. For nearly a year, Sohel took her from hospital to hospital across Dhaka in search of treatment. She died in March this year.

Yet the film reaches beyond one family's grief. Its characters face illness, poverty and uncertainty, but they keep fighting to live with dignity. Moving between tears and laughter, it explores how love and hope survive in the hardest circumstances.

'Hawar Gaari' was made quickly and on a modest budget. The script, locations, cast and crew were finalised in April and May, and shooting wrapped in Dhaka in June. Post-production began in July.

Most of the crew are Sohel's own students. Several established and emerging Bangladeshi artists joined the project willingly, and friends and well-wishers also lent their support.

Sohel wrote, directed, produced and edited the film himself. Sharafat Ali Shawkat was director of photography, and Belgian-Portuguese graphic designer Mika Barreto created the poster.

According to the filmmaker, film professionals at home and abroad who have seen the final rough cut have called it powerful and moving.

Sohel has dedicated the film to his late wife. He hopes it will raise awareness of cancer and support the Dr Shamrina Tanha Cancer Foundation, which is being set up in her memory.

He also hopes its distinctive storytelling and independent approach will enrich Bangladesh's film industry and inspire young filmmakers to make original work.

title_bn: Cape Verde votes in presidential election that could make history with first female president
title_en: Cape Verde votes in presidential election that could make history with first female president
summary_bn: With a population of around 500,000, Cape Verde is known for its competitive elections and peaceful transfers of power, a political tradition that remains uncommon in parts of West Africa.
summary_en: With a population of around 500,000, Cape Verde is known for its competitive elections and peaceful transfers of power, a political tradition that remains uncommon in parts of West Africa.
body_bn:
With a population of around 500,000, Cape Verde is known for its competitive elections and peaceful transfers of power, a political tradition that remains uncommon in parts of West Africa.

Cape Verdeans went to the polls on Sunday (15 November) in a presidential election that could make history by electing the country's first female head of state since gaining independence from Portugal in 1975.

Former Justice Minister Joana Rosa is contesting the election against incumbent President José Maria Neves, who is seeking a second five-year term. Six candidates are vying for the presidency. If none secures more than 50% of the vote, a run-off election will be held on 29 November.

Rosa is backed by the opposition Movement for Democracy (MpD), which governed the country for a decade before losing the parliamentary election in May. Although women have held senior positions in the Cabinet, the island nation has never had a female prime minister or president.

Under Cape Verde's parliamentary system, the prime minister exercises most executive powers and oversees government policy. The president, who is directly elected, largely performs a ceremonial role but has the authority to veto legislation.

With a population of around 500,000, Cape Verde is known for its competitive elections and peaceful transfers of power, a political tradition that remains uncommon in parts of West Africa.

Nearly 77,000 citizens living abroad are registered to vote, accounting for almost one-fifth of the country's total electorate.

Roselma Évora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde, said limited economic opportunities were prompting many young people to move abroad in search of better prospects.

She also noted that many voters felt disconnected from political leaders and wanted a president who could better understand the everyday challenges facing ordinary citizens.

Neves, who secured approximately 52% of the vote in the 2021 election, has pledged to work across party lines to improve housing, healthcare and education, generate employment and increase wages.

According to Évora, Neves has benefited from the greater public exposure that comes with holding the presidency, including among voters living overseas.

She said Rosa's candidacy was also challenging conventional perceptions of women's roles in a society that remains deeply patriarchal.

Rosa has made the need to maintain a balance of political power a central theme of her campaign. She argues that Cape Verde needs an institutional counterweight to the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde (PAICV), which supports Neves and currently controls the government and most municipalities.

PAICV secured a parliamentary majority in May, bringing an end to 10 years of administration by the Movement for Democracy. If Rosa wins, the presidency and the government would once again be controlled by opposing political camps.

However, Cape Verde-based writer Rosário Luz said political affiliations were likely to matter more to voters than Rosa's gender.

She observed that although women were well represented in politics, policies addressing their specific needs remained inadequate.

Women shoulder a significant share of household financial responsibilities in Cape Verde, but government policies have yet to adequately address the challenges they face, Luz added.

title_bn: 'Give me the home ministry for two weeks, I'll fix things,' says Asif Mahmud
title_en: 'Give me the home ministry for two weeks, I'll fix things,' says Asif Mahmud
summary_bn: Former adviser makes remark in Facebook post amid tension over political activities in Gopalganj.
summary_en: Former adviser makes remark in Facebook post amid tension over political activities in Gopalganj.
body_bn:
Former adviser makes remark in Facebook post amid tension over political activities in Gopalganj.

Former adviser Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain has said he could resolve the country's law and order situation if given responsibility for the Home Ministry for two weeks.

"If you cannot do it, give me the Home Ministry for two weeks. I'll fix things," he wrote in a Facebook post published at 3:27pm today (15 November).

His remark came amid growing concerns over a series of criminal incidents across the country, including crude bomb attacks, arson attacks, theft, snatching and other offences.

The post also came amid heightened tension in Gopalganj, where activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations staged processions, broke police barricades and allegedly vandalised a supershop earlier in the day.

Hundreds of activists reportedly gathered at different locations in the district town, chanting slogans in support of Awami League President Sheikh Hasina. They also set tyres on fire at several locations, prompting increased security deployment across the town.

The demonstrations disrupted normal activities, with shops temporarily closing and residents expressing concern over the situation.

Police, Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), Armed Police Battalion (APBn) and other law enforcement personnel were deployed to maintain order.

title_bn: Banned AL activists vandalise police vehicle, July memorial during procession in Gopalganj
title_en: Banned AL activists vandalise police vehicle, July memorial during procession in Gopalganj
summary_bn: DC withdrawn, SP transferred; 6 BGB platoons deployed.
summary_en: DC withdrawn, SP transferred; 6 BGB platoons deployed.
body_bn:
DC withdrawn, SP transferred; 6 BGB platoons deployed.

Leaders and activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations in Gopalganj today (15 November) vandalised an armoured personnel carrier (APC), a police box, a July memorial, university signage, and other public and private establishments while staging demonstrations in Gopalganj town.

The demonstrations and vandalism continued from 11am to 1:45pm, with hundreds of activists taking to the streets, chanting slogans in support of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and her party.

After evening, miscreants set ablaze a branch office of Grameen Bank in Ulpur area of Tungipara upazila, said Ayub Ali, officer-in-charge of Tungipara Police Station.

Besides, the police station's sub-inspector Moslem, who filed a case over the vandalism of a police vehicle on 10 November, was hacked by miscreants equipped with sharp weapons, the OC said, adding that the injured officer was hospitalised.

Gopalganj DC and SP transferred in latest administrative reshuffle DC withdrawn, SP transferred Amid protests and vandalism, district Deputy Commissioner (DC) Md Arif-uz-Zaman has been withdrawn, while Superintendent of Police (SP) Md Habibullah has been transferred to Feni.

Habiganj DC GM Sarfaraz has been made the new DC of Gopalganj while Arif has been attached to the public administration ministry. Feni SP Pratyush Kumar Majumder has been transferred to Gopalganj.

Four more senior police officials were transferred at the same time.

The changes were announced in separate notifications issued by the ministries of public administration and home affairs.

BGB deployment To maintain law and order in the district, six platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed.

The paramilitary members will perform duty alongside police, Special Response Battalion, Ansar, Armed Police Battalion (APBn) and other law enforcers, Brigadier General Mahmudul Hasan, brigade commander of Jashore region of the BGB, said at a press briefing in front of Gopalganj Circuit House in the afternoon.

Incidents of today According to sources, activists from different unions began gathering around 8am at the house of Salauddin Khan, organising secretary of Gopalganj municipality unit of the party, in Ghosherchar Uttarpara under Latifpur union of Gopalganj Sadar upazila. Food was also arranged for the participants there.

Led by Salauddin, the group entered the town through BSCIC Bridge. Another procession emerged from Ghosherchar Dakshinpara under the leadership of banned Chhatra League leader Md Samiul Haque Tanu, while separate groups arrived from the Mia and Nabinbagh areas under former Sadar municipality councillor Alamin.

Around noon, activists gathered near Shishu Park and the BSCIC area before marching through several parts of the town.

The processions passed through Launch Ghat, Women's College and Shilpakala Academy before converging near the old Launch Ghat Bridge. They then marched to the Awami League's district office in Bankpara, opened its long-locked doors.

Many protesters carried national flags and locally made weapons, including sticks, machetes, Chinese axes, spears, pikes and traditional oars and bamboo poles. The presence of women in the demonstrations was also noticeable.

During the demonstrations, protesters damaged the July Memorial Monument near Launch Ghat and vandalised the nameplate of Hadi Square at Gopalganj Science and Technology University, restoring its previous name, Joy Bangla Chattar.
body_en:
DC withdrawn, SP transferred; 6 BGB platoons deployed.

Leaders and activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations in Gopalganj today (15 November) vandalised an armoured personnel carrier (APC), a police box, a July memorial, university signage, and other public and private establishments while staging demonstrations in Gopalganj town.

The demonstrations and vandalism continued from 11am to 1:45pm, with hundreds of activists taking to the streets, chanting slogans in support of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and her party.

After evening, miscreants set ablaze a branch office of Grameen Bank in Ulpur area of Tungipara upazila, said Ayub Ali, officer-in-charge of Tungipara Police Station.

Besides, the police station's sub-inspector Moslem, who filed a case over the vandalism of a police vehicle on 10 November, was hacked by miscreants equipped with sharp weapons, the OC said, adding that the injured officer was hospitalised.

Gopalganj DC and SP transferred in latest administrative reshuffle DC withdrawn, SP transferred Amid protests and vandalism, district Deputy Commissioner (DC) Md Arif-uz-Zaman has been withdrawn, while Superintendent of Police (SP) Md Habibullah has been transferred to Feni.

Habiganj DC GM Sarfaraz has been made the new DC of Gopalganj while Arif has been attached to the public administration ministry. Feni SP Pratyush Kumar Majumder has been transferred to Gopalganj.

Four more senior police officials were transferred at the same time.

The changes were announced in separate notifications issued by the ministries of public administration and home affairs.

BGB deployment To maintain law and order in the district, six platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed.

The paramilitary members will perform duty alongside police, Special Response Battalion, Ansar, Armed Police Battalion (APBn) and other law enforcers, Brigadier General Mahmudul Hasan, brigade commander of Jashore region of the BGB, said at a press briefing in front of Gopalganj Circuit House in the afternoon.

Incidents of today According to sources, activists from different unions began gathering around 8am at the house of Salauddin Khan, organising secretary of Gopalganj municipality unit of the party, in Ghosherchar Uttarpara under Latifpur union of Gopalganj Sadar upazila. Food was also arranged for the participants there.

Led by Salauddin, the group entered the town through BSCIC Bridge. Another procession emerged from Ghosherchar Dakshinpara under the leadership of banned Chhatra League leader Md Samiul Haque Tanu, while separate groups arrived from the Mia and Nabinbagh areas under former Sadar municipality councillor Alamin.

Around noon, activists gathered near Shishu Park and the BSCIC area before marching through several parts of the town.

The processions passed through Launch Ghat, Women's College and Shilpakala Academy before converging near the old Launch Ghat Bridge. They then marched to the Awami League's district office in Bankpara, opened its long-locked doors.

Many protesters carried national flags and locally made weapons, including sticks, machetes, Chinese axes, spears, pikes and traditional oars and bamboo poles. The presence of women in the demonstrations was also noticeable.

During the demonstrations, protesters damaged the July Memorial Monument near Launch Ghat and vandalised the nameplate of Hadi Square at Gopalganj Science and Technology University, restoring its previous name, Joy Bangla Chattar.

title_bn: Govt sets up to Tk50 lakh grant ceiling for startups, opens door for NRBs
title_en: Govt sets up to Tk50 lakh grant ceiling for startups, opens door for NRBs
summary_bn: ICT Division policy introduces funding for startup ideas, prototypes, seed-stage ventures and investment readiness.
summary_en: ICT Division policy introduces funding for startup ideas, prototypes, seed-stage ventures and investment readiness.
body_bn:
ICT Division policy introduces funding for startup ideas, prototypes, seed-stage ventures and investment readiness.

The government will provide grants of up to Tk50 lakh, and even higher amounts in special cases, to early-stage startups to help young entrepreneurs turn innovative ideas into marketable products and services, create jobs, strengthen export capacity and attract domestic and foreign investment.

The grants will cover various stages of startup development, including idea generation, prototype development, pre-seed and seed funding, investment-readiness bridge funding and special innovation initiatives.

The ICT Division has issued a policy outlining the eligibility criteria and funding framework for the programme.

Under the policy, startups seeking investment-readiness, bridge and matching funds will be eligible for grants ranging from Tk10 lakh to Tk50 lakh.

For idea generation, grants will range from Tk1 lakh to Tk3 lakh. Individual applicants can receive up to Tk5 lakh for developing prototypes and minimum viable products (MVPs), while institutions will be eligible for up to Tk10 lakh for the same purpose.

Grants under special innovation programmes will be provided within limits determined by the government.

However, the policy allows the government to exceed the prescribed funding ceilings in specific cases.

"For strategically important, nationally prioritised or high-impact technology-based startups, the government may, if necessary, provide financial assistance exceeding the prescribed limits under any category," the policy states.

Both Bangladeshi citizens and non-resident Bangladeshis will be eligible for the grants.

However, individuals or organisations facing criminal proceedings involving embezzlement, corruption, fraud, money laundering or cybercrime will be disqualified from receiving the assistance.

Those who have previously misused government grants or failed to submit proper accounts or reports after receiving such funds will also be ineligible

body_bn:
Alok Healthcare and Hospital marked World Diabetes Day on 14 November, 2026 with a scientific seminar, a public awareness campaign and free medical camps in Dhaka's Mirpur.

Renata PLC and Incepta Pharmaceuticals supported the day-long programme, which aimed to raise awareness of diabetes prevention, early detection and treatment and help healthcare professionals share knowledge on managing the condition, according to the press release.

From 7am to 8am, hospital staff displayed banners and placards by the roadside to inform the public about diabetes risk factors, prevention, early detection and healthy living.

A continuing medical education seminar took place from noon to 1pm at Alok Mother and Child Care in Block A, Section 6, Mirpur. The chief guests were Professor Dr AKM Musa, a specialist in medicine, chest diseases, diabetes and rheumatology, and Dr Mahmudul Hossain, a specialist in diabetes, thyroid disorders and endocrinology. Both regularly see patients at Alok Healthcare Limited.

Specialists from the hospital spoke about diabetes prevention, early detection, current treatments and ways to prevent long-term complications.

Managing Director Md Lokman Hossain chaired the seminar and answered questions from journalists. Hospital Director Brigadier General (retired) Dr Sheikh Salahuddin and Deputy Director (Administration) Dr Mohammad Munir Mosharraf Khan also attended, alongside general managers, department heads, other officials, specialist doctors, journalists, media workers and patients.

The free medical camps ran from 8am to 2pm at Alok Healthcare's main branch in Mirpur-10 and Alok General Hospital in Mirpur-6. Patients, journalists and other media workers could receive free specialist consultations, blood pressure checks and tests, including fasting and random blood glucose tests, complete blood counts, HbA1c tests, serum creatinine tests and routine urine examinations.

The camps also offered discounts of up to 50% on other tests recommended by doctors and made free medicines available.

The hospital said public awareness, regular health checks, early diagnosis and appropriate treatment were important for preventing and managing diabetes.

title_en: ULAB honours journalism alumni with Best Achievers, Achiever of the Year awards
summary_bn: The University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) honoured its media studies and journalism alumni with Best Achievers and Achiever of the Year awards at its homecoming on 14 November, 2026. summary_en: The University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) honoured its media studies and journalism alumni with Best Achievers and Achiever of the Year awards at its homecoming on 14 November, 2026. The event brought together alumni, faculty members, students and guests for a programme that included showcases of alumni ventures
body_bn:
The University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh (ULAB) honoured its media studies and journalism alumni with Best Achievers and Achiever of the Year awards at its homecoming on 14 November, 2026.

The event brought together alumni, faculty members, students and guests for a programme that included showcases of alumni ventures, interactive activities and film screenings, according to the press release.

A roundtable titled "Changing Media Industry and the Coping Mechanism" explored changes in the media industry and how to adapt to them. A town hall titled "Reshaping the Future of MSJ Department" focused on the future of the Department of Media Studies and Journalism.

The evening programme at Forum Hall opened with a classical music performance by Shaibal Saha. Professor Shamsad Mortuza, vice-chancellor of ULAB, delivered the welcome address. Professor Sumon Rahman, dean of the School of Social Science and head of the Department of Media Studies and Journalism, gave a presentation.

Tanzim Ibn Wahab, director general of the Bangladesh National Museum, attended as chief guest. The award recipients spoke after the presentation ceremony.

Dr Mohammad Shazzad Hossain, the department's alumni relations coordinator, delivered the vote of thanks. The band AUSHOMAPTO closed the event with a musical performance.

title_en: Senior Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis killed in Gaza
summary_bn: Hamas' armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades, identified the slain commander as Samir Abu Younis, who led its Rafah Brigade and was involved in planning the group's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel, according to media reports.
summary_en: Hamas' armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades, identified the slain commander as Samir Abu Younis, who led its Rafah Brigade and was involved in planning the group's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel, according to media reports.
body_bn:
Hamas' armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades, identified the slain commander as Samir Abu Younis, who led its Rafah Brigade and was involved in planning the group's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel, according to media reports.

The Israeli military said today (15 November) that its forces had targeted a senior commander of Hamas' military wing, while the Palestinian group's armed wing confirmed the death of one of its commanders in Gaza.

The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) announced the strike in a post on X early today.

Hamas' armed wing, the Al-Qassam Brigades, identified the slain commander as Samir Abu Younis, who led its Rafah Brigade and was involved in planning the group's 7 October 2023 attack on Israel, according to media reports.

The Al-Qassam Brigades said Abu Younis was killed last evening. His funeral was scheduled to take place on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis.

title_bn: RMG unrest: 50 factories remain closed in Savar-Ashulia, 13 shut indefinitely in Gazipur
title_en: RMG unrest: 50 factories remain closed in Savar-Ashulia, 13 shut indefinitely in Gazipur
summary_bn: A total of 48 platoons of law enforcement personnel have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and protect factories.
summary_en: A total of 48 platoons of law enforcement personnel have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and protect factories.
body_bn:
A total of 48 platoons of law enforcement personnel have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and protect factories.

Authorities have shut 13 garment factories in Gazipur indefinitely amid ongoing labour unrest, while five others have declared a one-day general holiday today (15 November).

Meanwhile, the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt remained largely calm today, but more than 50 factories in the area remains closed for various reasons.

A total of 48 platoons of law enforcement personnel have been deployed across industrial areas in Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj to maintain law and order and protect factories.

The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) has deployed 35 platoons across the three areas, while five platoons of Ansar and eight platoons of the Special Response Battalion (SRB) have been deployed in Gazipur. The forces in Gazipur are being led by 25 executive magistrates.

According to a BGB press release issued today (15 November), 18 BGB platoons are performing security duties in Savar and Ashulia, 10 in different industrial areas of Gazipur and seven in Narayanganj.

According to industrial police and local sources, workers have been staging protests and work stoppages in different parts of Gazipur over the past few days, demanding, among other things, a minimum wage of Tk30,000.

This morning, workers gathered in front of a factory in the Mouchak area of Kaliakair. They left the area about half an hour after law enforcement personnel arrived. Isolated incidents of unrest were also reported in the Konabari and Jarun areas of Gazipur city.

Garment factories shut in Gazipur amid labour unrest. Photo: TBS "> Garment factories shut in Gazipur amid labour unrest. Photo: TBS In response, authorities declared 13 factories in the Mouchak and Konabari areas, including Interstoff Apparels Limited in the Palli Bidyut area of Kaliakair, closed indefinitely under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006.

Five other factories in the Mouchak, Konabari and Jarun areas declared a one-day general holiday.

Despite the unrest, production continues at most factories in Gazipur's industrial belt. Of the district's approximately 2,300 garment factories, only the 18 closed or holiday-declared factories have suspended operations.

Superintendent of Police of Gazipur Industrial Police Amjad Hossain said continuous labour unrest and work stoppages had forced factory authorities to close the 13 factories under the labour law. He added that the factories could reopen once the situation improved.

He said law enforcement agencies remained on high alert to prevent untoward incidents and protect lives and property in the industrial areas.

13 garment factories in Gazipur shut indefinitely amid labour unrest. Photo: TBS "> 13 garment factories in Gazipur shut indefinitely amid labour unrest. Photo: TBS Notably, garment factory owners yesterday (15 November) warned of indefinite closures – without pay – from today for factories where workers refuse to return to production.

Under Section 13(1) of the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006, workers are not entitled to wages or allowances for the duration their factories remain shut due to illegal strikes or unrest.

Meanwhile, despite reluctance among some members, the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) confirmed it will attend the minimum wage board meeting tomorrow (16 November) to submit its proposal.

However, the association warned that its participation in subsequent discussions will depend on how the situation on the ground unfolds.

title_en: BRAC University wraps up silver jubilee cultural competition with 33 finalists
summary_bn: BRAC University concluded its silver jubilee cultural competition on Thursday (12 November, 2026), with 33 finalists performing in 11 categories at its Merul Badda campus in Dhaka. summary_en: BRAC University concluded its silver jubilee cultural competition on Thursday (12 November, 2026), with 33 finalists performing in 11 categories at its Merul Badda campus in Dhaka. Nearly 300 students from across the university's departments took part in online auditions for "The Stage: Silver Jubilee Cultural Competit
body_bn:
BRAC University concluded its silver jubilee cultural competition on Thursday (12 November, 2026), with 33 finalists performing in 11 categories at its Merul Badda campus in Dhaka.

Nearly 300 students from across the university's departments took part in online auditions for "The Stage: Silver Jubilee Cultural Competition 2026", according to the press release.

Of those, 196 advanced to the theatre round, where faculty members and administrative staff judged their performances. Around 90 participants reached the semi-finals, where internal and external judges selected 33 finalists.

Hamin Ahmed of Miles attended the finale as a special guest. The top three finalists in each category performed before a panel of faculty members and professionals from various fields. Members of the judging panel also performed during the programme.

Tahmina Binta Zaman of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering won in acting, while Joyeta Moietree of the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering won in recitation.

Ahmed Adnan Khan of BRAC Business School won in both classical song and Nazrul Geeti. Avibadhan Das Arno and Kaoushik Debnath Joy, both of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, won in folk song and Rabindra Sangeet, respectively. Safawath Alam of BRAC Business School won in modern song.

Purnota Prachi of the Department of Biotechnology won in classical dance, while Rahatul Jannat of the Department of Pharmacy won in creative dance, which covered modern and contemporary styles. Hyperion won in band music, and Syed Ariful Islam Aowan of the Department of Microbiology won in instrumental performance.

BRAC University's Student Life team organised the competition as part of the university's silver jubilee celebrations. The university said the initiative supported the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 4 on quality education by encouraging creativity, artistic expression and learning beyond the classroom.
